title: cd-pipeline
description: A Kargo delivery pipeline per project. Strict throughout: a key the chart does not read is refused rather than ignored, because a typo in a value that decides what is promoted renders cleanly and promotes the wrong thing. With no projects nothing is rendered.

labels.description: Labels on every object. None by default: the chart adds nothing the values do not say.

annotations.description: Annotations on every object, beside the sync-wave. None by default.

waves.description: The Argo CD sync-wave of each kind of object.

namespace.description: Where the Argo CD Applications of the Stages live.

repoURL.description: The repository a promotion writes the pin to.

secretName.description: The Secret each project namespace gets (default `kargo-git-writeback`).

remoteKey.description: The key in the store that holds the GitHub App's credentials.

properties.description: The property of that key each credential is read from.

credentials.description: An ExternalSecret in each project namespace that produces the git credentials Kargo writes back with (a GitHub App).

pinFile.description: The file the pin is written to, relative to the repository; tokens {stage}, {project}, {slug}, {product} (the slug), {pinKey} and, where the project gives them, {vendor} and {customer}.

pinKey.description: The key written in it; the same tokens.

commitMessage.description: The same tokens and {version}, the Kargo expression for the promoted version.

seedPinFile.description: Seed a missing pin file: before yaml-update, a file-write step (alias seed-pin, overwrite false, continueOnError true) writes the pin file with every key this Stage writes, each "" (dormant), so a Stage's first promotion into a folder with no pin file succeeds. An existing file is never changed: on every later promotion the step fails with "already exists", which continueOnError ignores, and the Promotion succeeds. It adds no key to an existing file. Default false.

jobs.description: What every verification Job is run as.

image.description: An image with a shell and curl.

jqImage.description: An image holding /jq, mounted as an image volume.

script.description: Replaces the script the chart ships.

gateImage.description: The promotion-gate image (ghcr.io/truvity/cd/promotion-gate). Set: the promoted-version check runs its Go check, `/ko-app/promotion-gate promoted-version`, with no script ConfigMap and no jq volume, and needs neither `image` nor `jqImage`. Empty (the default): the shell script.

objects.description: false: a Stage names the check, and its ServiceAccount, Role, RoleBinding and AnalysisTemplate are rendered by the cluster's owner under the same names, not here.

false: a Stage names its gate, `<slug>-<stage>-metrics-gate`, and the gate's ServiceAccount, ConfigMap and AnalysisTemplate are rendered by the cluster's owner under the same names, not here; none of the other settings is read then.

gateImage.description: The promotion-gate image (ghcr.io/truvity/cd/promotion-gate). Set: the gate runs `/ko-app/promotion-gate metrics-gate`, with no script ConfigMap and no jq volume. Empty (the default): the shell script.

image.description: An image with a shell and curl; default promotedVersion.image.

jqImage.description: An image holding /jq, mounted as an image volume; default promotedVersion.jqImage.

serviceAccount.description: The ServiceAccount the Job runs as; tokens {stage}, {slug}, {project}.

issuerHost.description: The host of the issuer the Job exchanges its ServiceAccount token at (`https://<host>/token`).

url.description: The query endpoint's base URL; queries go to <url>/api/v1/query.

caBundle.description: Verify the endpoint with caBundle's root (mounted, and passed as CA_BUNDLE).

endpoints.description: Stage name -> the endpoint the gate of that Stage reads.

audience.description: The audience the projected ServiceAccount token is minted for.

phase1Seconds.description: How long to wait for the promoted version to be the only one serving.

bakeSeconds.description: How long, from the ready point, the bake may take to collect minJourneys clean samples.

upstreams.description: Stage -> the Stages it may promote from, in preference; the first the project has wins.

applicationName.description: The Argo CD Application a derived Stage watches; tokens {stage}, {app}, {project}, {slug}, {product} (the slug) and, where the project gives them, {vendor} and {customer}.

stageName.description: The name of a Stage of a customer's chain (`projects[].customers`), with the tokens `{stage}` (the Stage of `stageOrder`), `{customer}` and, with `projects[].components`, `{component}`; default `{stage}-{customer}`, or `{stage}-{customer}-{component}` with components.

promotedVersion.description: Every derived Stage runs the promoted-version check.

claims.description: The claims of each approver subject; tokens {stage}, {slug}, {project} in every string.
The claims of the admin subject; tokens {slug}, {project} in every string.

graph.description: The promotion graph a project with `stageOrder` derives its Stages and access from.

global.description: Also render the namespace and the ServiceAccount that carries these claims.

viewer.description: Read access for every user the ServiceAccount's claims match: a RoleBinding in each project.

name.description: The Project, its namespace and, unless `warehouse.name` says otherwise, its Warehouse. Renaming one deletes it and the Freight history it holds.

slug.description: Names the checks and fills {slug}; default the project's name.

vendor.description: Who makes the product: the {vendor} token of this project's name templates (promotion.pinFile, pinKey, commitMessage, prTitle; graph.applicationName). A template that names {vendor} without it is refused.

customer.description: Whom this installation is for: the {customer} token, as vendor.

pinKey.description: Fills {pinKey}: the key the promoted version is written under.

repoURL.description: The repository this project's promotions write the pin to; replaces the release's `git.repoURL`.

oneOf.description: `false`: no write-back credentials for this project's namespace.

secretName.description: The Secret each project namespace gets (default `kargo-git-writeback`).

remoteKey.description: The key in the store that holds the GitHub App's credentials.

properties.description: The property of that key each credential is read from.

oneOf.description: An ExternalSecret in each project namespace that produces the git credentials Kargo writes back with (a GitHub App).

credentials.description: This project's write-back credentials (an ExternalSecret in its namespace); replaces the release's `git.credentials`. `false` renders none for this project.

git.description: Per-project override of the release's `git`: a project may write to its own repository with its own credentials.

pinFile.description: The file the pin is written to, relative to the repository; tokens {stage}, {project}, {slug}, {pinKey}.

pinKey.description: The key written in it; the same tokens.

commitMessage.description: The same tokens and {version}, the Kargo expression for the promoted version.

seedPinFile.description: The release's promotion.seedPinFile, for this project.

promotion.description: Per-project override of the release's `promotion`, with the same keys: a key set here replaces the release's (`retry` and `gate` merge key by key).

name.description: The chart's name in an index repository; none for an OCI one.

versionPrefix.description: Written in front of the version in the pin, for a repository whose tags carry one.

subscribeAs.description: How the Warehouse discovers the chart. `chart` (default) is a chart subscription. `image` is an image subscription with SemVer selection and `strictSemvers: false`, for an OCI chart whose tags carry a `v` (Helm's tag listing drops them, so a chart subscription finds nothing). A leading `oci://` is dropped from `repoURL` for the subscription, the promotion steps write the discovered tag as it is (the `v` stays), and `name` and `versionPrefix` are refused.

pin.description: What the promotion writes as the pin. `tag` (default) is the discovered version or tag. `digest` is the artifact's digest (`imageFrom(...).Digest`), for an artifact that is deployed by what it is rather than by what it is called; it needs `subscribeAs: image`, refuses `versionPrefix`, `name` and any promoted-version check (there is no chart version in the Application to compare), and adds a `{tag}` token to `promotion.commitMessage` and `promotion.prTitle`.

strictSemvers.description: The image subscription's `strictSemvers`, with `subscribeAs: image`. Unset keeps `false`; a Warehouse whose live object has Kargo's own default (`true`) sets it, so the spec does not differ from the stored object forever.

pinKey.description: The key the companion's pin is written under, in the same pin file and commit as the chart's: a template with the tokens of `promotion.pinKey`. Default the chart's filled key with `-<companion>` after it (`pins.dev-web` beside `pins.dev`).

additionalProperties.description: The companion's artifact from that source, laid over the companion's own keys (usually `repoURL`, and `semver` for its prerelease line).

sources.description: The companion from a further source, by the source's name (a key of `sources`): each Warehouse of that source (`<warehouse>-<source>`, or a customer's `<warehouse>-<customer>-<source>`) subscribes to it in place of the companion, and its Stages promote it. A source not named here subscribes to the companion as it is.

additionalProperties.description: An artifact promoted with the chart: the same keys as `chart`, and `pinKey`.

companions.description: Further artifacts that move with the chart in one Freight, by name, such as a static bundle released beside an api chart. Every Warehouse of the project (its own, each source's and each customer's) subscribes to the chart and to every companion, so a new version of either makes one Freight that holds both, and the pair that reaches a later Stage is the pair that ran on the one before. Each Stage writes the chart's pin and one pin per companion in one `yaml-update` of the pin file, so in one commit. A companion's repository must differ from the chart's and from every other companion's. Not with `warehouse.subscriptions` (verbatim) or spelled-out `promotionTemplate`s. With the promoted-version check on, each companion has a check of its own beside the chart's (`<slug>-<stage>-promoted-<companion>`, argument `<companion>-digest` or `<companion>-version`), so a part none of the Stage's Applications renders fails on its own; a companion pinned by digest is judged by its artifact in the Applications' Helm values. A project with companions may have no `chart`: its Warehouses subscribe to the companions alone, its Stages write and check their pins alone, and an end-to-end check or a metrics gate is refused; its customers then name no chart, and a source names only its companions (`companions.<name>.sources.<source>`).

customers.description: Derived Stages only (`stageOrder`): the customers of a product that one Kargo Project delivers. Each customer gets a Warehouse `<warehouse>-<customer>` on the project's `chart` (or its own `chart`) and its own chain of Stages, one for each Stage of `stageOrder`, named by `graph.stageName`; a customer's Stages request only its Warehouse, promote only from its own Stages, and the first of its chain promotes on its own. The project renders no Warehouse of its own. `{stage}` in Application names and pins stays the Stage of `stageOrder`, and `{customer}` is the customer. With `sources`, each customer also gets a Warehouse `<warehouse>-<customer>-<source>` for each source, and the customer's Stage of a Stage that `stageSources` names takes it: a customer's preview builds on its first Stage, its releases on the next.

sources.description: This customer's chart from a further source, by the source's name (a key of `sources`): its Warehouse `<warehouse>-<customer>-<source>` subscribes to it. A source not named here gives the customer the project's `sources.<source>`.

components.description: With `components` (required there): the components this customer takes, each a key of `components`. One chain of Stages for each. Not every customer takes every component.

source.description: A source of each component the customer takes (`components.<component>.sources`): the lane's Stages take `<warehouse>-<component>-<source>`.

name.description: The lane's name, default `source`: the customer is named `<customer>-<name>`, and the promotion's `{customerBase}` is `<customer>` and `{lanePath}` `<name>/` (for a pin file `<customer>/<lane>/<component>/`).

stage.description: The lane's one Stage: the first Stage of `stageOrder` (the default), and no other.

lane.description: With `components`: this customer is a lane, a preview of its components from a further source. Its chain is one Stage, the first of `stageOrder`, which takes the components' Warehouses of `source`, promotes on its own and promotes nothing onward. The customer must be named `<customer>-<lane>` (`lane.name`, default `source`), so its Stages, Applications and pin keys are its own; in the pin file, commit message and pull request title `{customerBase}` is `<customer>` and `{lanePath}` is `<lane>/` (`""` and the customer itself for a customer that is not a lane), and the default pin file is `versions/{customerBase}/{lanePath}{component}/{stage}.yaml`.

additionalProperties.description: The component's chart from a further source: its own Warehouse, <warehouse>-<component>-<source>, that a lane customer (customers[].lane.source) takes. The same keys as `chart`.

sources.description: The component's further sources, by name: each one a Warehouse <warehouse>-<component>-<source>, for the lane customers whose lane names the source.

components.description: Derived Stages only (`stageOrder`), with `customers`: a product made of several parts, each one a chart of its own, delivered by one Kargo Project for several customers. Each component has one Warehouse, `<warehouse>-<component>`, shared by every customer that takes it, and one of each of its sources, `<warehouse>-<component>-<source>`; the project renders no Warehouse of its own and no customer's. Each customer takes the components it lists (`customers[].components`), a chain of Stages for each, one for each Stage of `stageOrder`, named by `graph.stageName` (default `{stage}-{customer}-{component}`, which must name both). `{component}` fills Application names, pins and the promotion's wording beside `{customer}`. Not with `chart`, `sources`, `stageSources` or `companions`.

expression.description: A Kargo expression (expr-lang) that must be true for the Warehouse to create Freight from a discovery, for instance `imageFrom('repo-a')?.Tag == imageFrom('repo-b')?.Tag`.

freightCreationCriteria.description: Kargo's `Warehouse.spec.freightCreationCriteria`, on the project's own Warehouse (`chart`); not on the Warehouses of `sources`.

claims.description: The OIDC claims a token must carry; Kargo maps a matching token to this ServiceAccount.

approve.description: May also approve Freight, which Kargo scopes to the whole project.

approvers.description: Derive one approver subject per Stage after the first (graph.approvers); needs stageOrder.

admins.description: Derive one admin subject that promotes every Stage and approves (graph.admins); needs stageOrder.

name.description: The Stage's name, and the name the access rules and `from` refer to it by.

from.description: The Stage whose verified Freight this Stage promotes. Absent: the Stage takes Freight straight from the Warehouse (the project's first).

source.description: The source (a key of the project's `sources`) the Stage takes Freight from and installs from. Absent: the project's `chart`. A Stage and its upstream take the same source.

autoPromote.description: Promote new Freight without waiting for a person.

noAutoPromote.description: The ProjectConfig names the Stage with autoPromotionEnabled false, over `autoPromote`: what a derived Stage that the project's `noAutoPromote` lists is marked with.

noPrereleases.description: The Stage takes releases only: its promotion starts with a `fail` step for the chart and for each companion, which refuses a version that has a prerelease part (`1.4.0-rc.1`). What a derived Stage that the project's `noPrereleases` lists is marked with. Not with `promotionTemplate`.

applications.description: The Argo CD Applications this Stage deploys, by name. A Stage that promotes from this one waits for them to be Healthy and Synced; its own promoted-version check reads them.

mode.description: How the pin reaches the repository: a pull request that must merge (default when the Stage has an upstream) or a push to the branch (default for the first Stage).

promotedVersion.description: Verify that the Stage's Applications render the promoted chart version (needs `applications`, and `promotedVersion.gateImage` or `promotedVersion.image` and `.jqImage`).

metric.description: Name of the one metric the template measures (default `check`).

args.description: The AnalysisTemplate's argument names; default `[chart-version]`, the version the Stage's Freight promoted.

serviceAccount.description: The ServiceAccount the Job runs as.

createServiceAccount.description: Render the ServiceAccount (default true); false when it exists elsewhere.

configMap.description: Name of the ConfigMap that holds the script.

file.description: Key and file name of the script (default `verify.sh`).

script.description: A script mounted read-only at /scripts. With no `command`, it is run with /bin/sh.

env.description: Values are strings. Argo Rollouts substitutes `{{args.<name>}}` in them.

volumes.description: Pod volumes, verbatim, after the script's.

volumeMounts.description: Container mounts, verbatim, after the script's.

items.description: A Job check: an AnalysisTemplate whose measurement is one Job, run once, decided by its exit code.

analysisTemplates.description: Names of AnalysisTemplates that exist already, run beside the rest.

metricsGate.description: Run the built-in metrics gate (`metricsGate`) before the Stage's own checks.

promotionTemplate.description: The Stage's promotion template, verbatim; replaces the built-in git promotion.

e2eApplication.description: The Argo CD Application that runs the product's end-to-end suite as a sync hook. The Stage's promotion ends with an `argocd-update` step that syncs it and waits, and a verification check reads the operation. The Application must carry `kargo.akuity.io/authorized-stage` for this Stage and is not listed in `applications`. Needs `promotedVersion.image` and `.jqImage`.

createProject.description: Render the project's cluster-scoped `Project` (default). `false` renders everything else of the project in its namespace and no `Project`: for an installation where one party owns the Project (and so the namespace) and another the Warehouse, Stages and access in it. `annotations` are refused with it.

annotations.description: Annotations on the Project object alone, beside the chart-wide ones (for instance Kargo's `kargo.akuity.io/keep-namespace: "true"`, which makes deleting a Project leave its namespace and the Freight in it).

stageOrder.description: Derive the Stages, in this order, from the promotion graph (`graph`) instead of spelling `stages` out.

upstreams.description: Replaces graph.upstreams for the Stages it names.

autoPromote.description: Derived Stages that promote on their own although they have an upstream.

noAutoPromote.description: Derived Stages that do not promote on their own, whatever `autoPromote` and the no-upstream rule say; each one a Stage of stageOrder. The ProjectConfig names them with autoPromotionEnabled false.

noPrereleases.description: Derived Stages that take releases only; each one a Stage of stageOrder. Their promotion refuses a version with a prerelease part, so a release candidate an earlier Stage ran cannot be promoted into them.

stageSources.description: Stage -> the source (a key of `sources`) it takes Freight from, for derived Stages. A Stage it does not name takes `chart`.

applications.description: The applications every derived Stage watches, through graph.applicationName; default the slug.

applicationsByStage.description: Replaces `applications` for the Stages it names.

e2eStages.description: Derived Stages whose promotion runs the end-to-end Application.

e2eApplication.description: The end-to-end application, through graph.applicationName; default <slug>-e2e.

metricsGateStages.description: Derived Stages that run the metrics gate.

namespace.description: The workload's namespace; default the slug.

release.description: The workload's Helm release; default the slug.

e2eJobRequired.description: The version's own e2e Job must succeed (default true).

appProjects.description: Argo CD AppProjects, by name, rendered in `argocd.namespace` beside the pipeline: the projects whose Applications the Stages watch. Each entry's `spec` is the AppProject spec verbatim. Neither the chart-wide `labels` nor `annotations` apply to them (those guard Kargo objects).

global.description: Helm's own: a parent chart's global values reach every subchart (cd-project packages this chart). The chart reads none of it.
